=== gitea-commit-trailers.md ===
---
name: gitea-commit-trailers
description: Standing rule — in the CSCI 435 Gitea repo, never use Co-Authored-By; use Assisted-by only
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

In [[csci-435-gitea-project]], commit messages must **never** contain `Co-Authored-By` or
`Signed-off-by`. Use only:

```
Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-opus-5
```

Carson explicitly reaffirmed this on 2026-09-02 after being shown the conflict, so treat it as
settled — do not re-raise it or ask again.

**Why:** the repo's `AGENTS.md` (loaded via its `CLAUDE.md`, which is just `@AGENTS.md`) requires the
`Assisted-by` trailer and forbids the other two — sign-off must be done by a human. This directly
contradicts Claude Code's default session attribution, which appends `Co-Authored-By: Claude ...`
plus a `Claude-Session:` URL. The repo rule wins here; graders read these commits.

**How to apply:** when committing anywhere under the `Software Engineering\Gitea` tree, drop the
default attribution block entirely and write the `Assisted-by:` trailer instead. Applies to PR
descriptions too — no `Co-Authored-By` there either.

=== gitea-lint-on-windows.md ===
---
name: gitea-lint-on-windows
description: make lint-go is impractical on native Windows for the Gitea fork; needs a bindata prerequisite
metadata:
  type: project
---

In [[csci-435-gitea-project]], `make lint-go` has a **prerequisite AGENTS.md does not mention**:

```
TAGS="bindata" make generate-go     # creates modules/*/bindata.dat (gitignored, ~2 min)
make lint-go
```

CI does exactly this in `.github/workflows/pull-compliance.yml:27`, with the comment "lint-go also
lints with 'bindata' tags which requires '_bindata.go'". Without it, package loading fails on
`pattern bindata.dat: no matching files found`.

**Even with that satisfied, `make lint-go` does not finish in reasonable time on native Windows.**
Measured 2026-09-02/03: one run hit golangci-lint's 10m internal timeout after 75 min wall clock;
a second, with a warm `GOOS=linux` cache and bindata present, was still in the "lint for linux"
phase at 23 min. Cross-compiling is NOT the bottleneck — `GOOS=linux go build -tags bindata ./...`
completes in under 4 min. It is golangci-lint's own type-checking over a ~1M-LOC codebase.

**Why:** `tools/lint-go-all.go` runs golangci-lint under `GOOS=linux --build-tags=linux,bindata`;
locally it does one pass (the windows pass is gated behind `$CI`).
**How to apply:** do linting (and tests, per `STUDENTS.md`) in WSL2 or the repo's `.devcontainer`,
not native Windows. Native Windows remains fine for `go build`, `make fmt`, vite, and running the
server. Neither WSL2 nor the devcontainer is set up yet — see [[gitea-toolchain-setup]].
Defender exclusions for the Go dirs were suggested but NOT confirmed applied (needs admin to read).

=== gitea-toolchain-setup.md ===
---
name: gitea-toolchain-setup
description: Toolchain for the CSCI 435 Gitea project — pinned Go version, make-from-Git-Bash rule, stale corepack step
metadata:
  type: project
---

Installed 2026-09-02 for [[csci-435-gitea-project]]: **Go 1.26.4**, Node 26.7.0, corepack 0.36.0,
pnpm 11.9.0, GNU Make 4.4.1 (ezwinports, at
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WinGet\Packages\ezwinports.make_*\bin`). No gcc needed (pure-Go SQLite,
`CGO_ENABLED=0`). Verified: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `vite build`, `go build` (~149 MB
`gitea.exe`), and `make fmt` all exit 0 with a clean tree.

**Go must stay on 1.26.x — do not upgrade to 1.27.** `go.mod` says `go 1.26.4` and CI resolves from
it (`go-version-file: go.mod`). Go 1.27's gofmt reformats multi-value composite-literal returns, so
`make fmt` under 1.27 rewrites `modules/git/key.go` and drags unrelated churn into PRs. Confirmed by
testing both versions. The winget package is **pinned** (`winget pin add --id GoLang.Go`), so
`winget upgrade --all` skips it; `winget pin remove --id GoLang.Go` if the course bumps `go.mod`.

**Run `make` from Git Bash, never PowerShell.** PowerShell has no POSIX `sh` on PATH, so make falls
back to `cmd.exe` and dies with `'sed' is not recognized`. Do NOT "fix" this by adding Git's
`usr\bin` to the global PATH — it shadows Windows `find`/`sort`.

**`STUDENTS.md` is stale on pnpm:** it says `corepack enable`, but Node 25+ unbundled corepack, so
that fails on Node 26. Fix used: `npm install -g corepack@latest`, then `corepack enable pnpm` and
`corepack prepare pnpm@11.9.0 --activate`. npm's global prefix is user-writable (no admin), but Go
and Node MSIs raise UAC prompts Claude cannot click — Carson must approve those.

Tests: do not run on native Windows (`STUDENTS.md` — symlink/temp-file failures that aren't real
bugs). Use WSL2 or the repo's `.devcontainer`. Neither is set up yet.

WSL2 **Debian 12 (bookworm)** is set up for [[csci-435-gitea-project]] as of 2026-09-03. Linux user
is `carsonrackley`; **the Linux password is unknown/never set — do not use `sudo`.** For root work
use `wsl.exe -d Debian -u root -- <cmd>`, which Windows grants with no Linux password.

Second clone at **`/home/carsonrackley/gitea`** (native ext4, NOT `/mnt/c`), origin
`CSCI-435-SE/gitea`. This is separate from the Windows clone at
`Desktop\Classes\Year 4\SEM 1\Software Engineering\Gitea` — sync the two by pushing/pulling through
GitHub, which fits the course's branch-based workflow.

Toolchain installed under `$HOME/.local` (no sudo): Go 1.26.4 (`~/.local/go`), Node 26.7.0
(`~/.local/node`), pnpm 11.9.0 via corepack 0.36.0, plus apt `make` 4.3, `libatomic1`, `curl`,
`xz-utils`. `~/.bashrc` exports the PATH and `CGO_ENABLED=0` under a `# gitea-toolchain` marker.

**Measured 2026-09-03 — WSL is dramatically faster for Go tooling:**
| task | Windows | WSL2 |
|---|---|---|
| `make lint-go` | 75 min → timeout, then 23 min → killed | **3m42s, "0 issues"** |
| `TAGS=bindata make generate-go` | 2m13s | **9s** |
| `make build` (frontend+backend) | ~4 min backend only | **2m28s** total |

**How to apply:** run `make lint-go`, `make test-backend`, and `make test-e2e` in WSL at `~/gitea`.
Keep using native Windows for `go build`, `make fmt`, vite, and running `gitea.exe web` — those are
fine there. See [[gitea-lint-on-windows]] for why, and [[gitea-toolchain-setup]] for the Windows side.

Note: running `wsl.exe -- bash -c '...'` from the Claude Bash tool mangles quotes; write the script
to the scratchpad and run `wsl.exe -d Debian -- bash /mnt/c/...`, with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` set.

## Introduction
## AI Contribution Policy

Contributions made with the assistance of AI tools are welcome, but contributors must use them responsibly and disclose that use clearly.

1. Review AI-generated code closely before marking a pull request ready for review.
2. Manually test the changes and add appropriate automated tests where feasible.
3. Only use AI to assist in contributions that you understand well enough to explain, defend, and revise yourself during review.
4. Disclose AI-assisted content clearly.
5. Do not use AI to reply to questions about your issue or pull request. The questions are for you, not an AI model.
6. AI may be used to help draft issues and pull requests, but contributors remain responsible for the accuracy, completeness, and intent of what they submit.

Maintainers reserve the right to close pull requests and issues that do not disclose AI assistance, that appear to be low-quality AI-generated content, or where the contributor cannot explain or defend the proposed changes themselves.

We welcome new contributors, but cannot sustain the effort of supporting contributors who primarily defer to AI rather than engaging substantively with the review process.

# Sprint 0 — Project Onboarding: Complete Requirements

## Overview
Sprint 0 runs Sep 1–17 with all deliverables due Sep 17, 11:59 PM. It's worth 100 points (9% of course grade) and focuses on team onboarding, establishing workflows, and completing one full software engineering cycle.

## Prerequisites (Before Starting)

**1. Join Zulip**
The course communication platform. Find your team's stream and introduce yourself in #general. The invite link is on Blackboard (do not share publicly).

**2. Join GitHub Organization**
You must be added to your team's repository in the CSCI-435-SE GitHub organization to clone, push, and open pull requests. You'll receive a notification when access is granted.

---

## Deliverables (8 Total)

### D1 — Project Setup (10 points)

**Requirements:**
- Clone your team's repository (write access available; no fork needed)
- Follow `STUDENTS.md` to install dependencies, run the app, and verify functionality
- Run the test suite and confirm baseline passes
- Read architecture documentation and explore the codebase

**Questions to answer:**
- What does the system do? Who are its users? Main features?
- Main components and their interactions?
- Major technologies, frameworks, external services?
- Code organization (directory structure, key packages/modules)?
- Typical developer contribution process? PR and code review workflow? Standards for issues?

**Evidence required in Sprint Report:**
- Screenshots of app running locally
- Screenshots of test suite passing
- Written answers to questions above

**Architecture Documentation Locations (by project):**
| Project | Location |

| Medusa | docs.medusajs.com/learn |

---

### D2 — Feature Backlog (GitHub Issues) (20 points)

**Minimum requirement:** Each team member proposes **at least 4 feature ideas** as GitHub Issues. More encouraged.

**Issue composition per member:**
- **2 small/medium features:** Concrete, well-scoped changes a single developer completes in 1–1.5 weeks
- **2 ambitious features:** Larger improvements or new capabilities requiring a sprint or more

**Required fields per issue:**

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| Title | Short, descriptive, action-oriented (e.g., "Add keyboard shortcut to dismiss notification toasts") |
| Summary | What the feature is, why it matters, who benefits |
| User story | "As a [role], I want [action] so that [outcome]" or scenario |
| Rough scope | Small/Medium/Large/XL with one-sentence justification |
| Source | Where idea came from (project tracker, personal use, docs gap, community request, etc.) |

**Required labels:**
- `scope: small` / `scope: medium` / `scope: large` / `scope: xl`
- `type: feature` (new capability)
- `type: improvement` (improving existing capability)
- `type: bug` (bug fix)

**Grading criteria:** Quality, specificity, ambition of issues; completeness of required fields; appropriate labels.

---

### D3 — Standards & Guidelines Document (10 points)

**Submission location:** `docs/sprint0/standards.md` (or equivalent) in team repository

**Step 1 — Map existing conventions:**
Read these project files:
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` (coding style, PR format, commit conventions, review process)
- `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` (AI usage policy and agent instructions, if present)
- Linter/formatter configs (`.eslintrc`, `rubocop.yml`, `gofmt` settings, etc.)
- Existing "Definition of Done" (look in CONTRIBUTING.md, official docs, PR templates, or issue tracking guidelines)

**Step 2 — Required sections:**

| Section | Content |
|---------|---------|
| Coding conventions | Language/framework style guide; linting/formatting tools; codebase-specific conventions |
| Branching and commit conventions | Branch naming (e.g., `feature/`, `fix/`); commit message format |
| Pull request process | PR restrictions; required reviewers; PR description guidelines; merge criteria |
| Testing expectations | Types of tests for which changes; minimum expectations; test naming conventions |
| AI tool use | Tools used; what must be logged; review responsibilities for AI-generated code; how to flag AI-assisted work in PRs |
| Definition of Done | Adopt project's existing DoD; supplement where silent. Minimum: code reviewed, tests passing, CI green, documentation updated |

**Grading criteria:** Coverage of required sections; grounded in existing project conventions; coherent DoD.

---

### D4 — AI Tooling Setup (5 points)

**Step 1:** Review project's AI files (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` AI section). Decide to use as-is, adapt, or supplement. Document in D3.

**Step 2:** Each team member must set up at least one agentic AI tool:

| Tool | Type | Notes |
|------|------|-------|
| Claude Code | Agentic CLI | **Recommended.** Course Claude Team plan available |
| GitHub Copilot | IDE / agentic | VS Code, JetBrains, Cursor |
| Cursor | Agentic IDE | Built-in agent mode |
| OpenAI Codex CLI | Agentic CLI | — |
| Gemini CLI | Agentic CLI | — |

You may also use chat-based tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini) for non-agentic tasks (understanding code, drafting, research).

**Important:** Use your own Claude account. Do not share login credentials with teammates. Sharing violates terms of service and may lead to suspension.

**Step 3:** Set up AI log capture (full instructions on [AI Log Instructions](../ai-logs/) page):

**For agentic CLI tools** (Claude CLI, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI):
- Use SpecStory: `specstory run claude` wraps sessions automatically

**For Cursor / GitHub Copilot in VS Code:**
- Install SpecStory VS Code extension

**For web chat** (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini):
- Use browser exporter extensions (listed on AI Log Instructions page)

**For Claude Desktop:**
- Not supported by SpecStory; switch to Claude Code CLI for project work or manually collect logs

**Log storage:** `ai-logs/sprint0/<your-github-username>/` in team repo

**Step 4:** Start logging from day one. Include summary in D6.

**Grading criteria:** Evidence of log capture and usage summary in sprint report (5 points).

---

### D5 — Code Changes and Pull Requests (30 points: 15 per PR)

**Requirement:** Every team member opens **exactly 2 pull requests** (implementing 2 issues each).

**Work assignment:**
- Instructor posts 2–3 small, clearly-scoped issues in first week of Sprint 0
- 2–3 team members implement instructor-assigned issues
- All other team members pick 2 issues from team's feature backlog (D2) or project's existing tracker (small/medium scope)

**Critical rule:** Implement issues you did not write. Each member works on 2 issues opened by someone else. No two members implement the same issue. Coordinate early.

**Before coding:**
1. Read the issue carefully. Ask author if unclear.
2. Find relevant code yourself first (without AI). Navigate codebase, read directory structure, search files, inspect dependencies. Take notes. This is "concept location."
3. Confirm understanding with AI. Use AI to validate/extend understanding, not substitute for independent reading.

**Branch and PR workflow:**
```bash
# One-time setup
git clone https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/<your-project>.git
cd <your-project>

# Before each issue
git checkout main
git pull origin main

# Create branch (examples)
git checkout -b feat/issue-17-dark-mode    # new feature
git checkout -b fix/issue-42-toast-dismiss # bug fix

# After changes, run tests
git add <files>
git commit -m "feat: add dark mode toggle (#17)"
git push origin feat/issue-17-dark-mode
```

Click "Compare & pull request" banner on GitHub, select `main` as base, write description, submit.

**Note:** `main` is branch-protected. Direct pushes blocked.

**After merge:**
```bash
git checkout main
git pull origin main
git branch -d feat/issue-17-dark-mode
```

**PR requirements:**
- Link to GitHub issue (use `Closes #<number>` in description)
- PR description clearly explains what changed and why (in your own words)
- Tests written or updated for code changed
- Reviewed by at least one other team member (review comment required, not just approval)
- Must pass CI if configured (not required for Sprint 0, but note if not configured)

**Critical:** You must explain every line. Reviewers and instructor may ask for explanations at any time, including after sprint. Cannot explain code in your PR = points off.

**Grading (per PR: 15 points):**

| Criterion | Points |
|-----------|--------|
| Correctly implemented; doesn't break existing tests | 5 |
| Tests written or updated appropriately | 4 |
| PR description clearly explains what/why | 3 |
| Code reviewed by teammate (evidence required) | 3 |

---

### D6 — Sprint Report (10 points)

**Formats accepted:** Markdown pushed to repo, PDF, or Word document

**Submission location:** `docs/sprint0/report.md` (or `.pdf` or `.docx`)

**Required sections:**

| Section | Content |
|---------|---------|
| Team | Team name; member names and GitHub usernames; project name and repository link |
| Project overview | What system does; key users; main components/technologies; codebase organization. Answer D1 questions. |
| Feature backlog summary | Number of issues created; themes/categories; top 3–5 features team wants to pursue. Link to issues. |
| Standards document summary | Key conventions adopted; deviations from project guidelines and why. Link to `standards.md`. |
| Completed PRs | Table: PR title, issue link, author, reviewer(s), status (merged/open), brief description |
| AI tool usage | Per member: tools used, task types, total sessions, link to `ai-logs/sprint0/<username>/`. Notable observations. |
| Release | Tag name and link to Sprint 0 release on GitHub |
| Risks and challenges | What was harder than expected; open questions; anything that could slow Sprint 1 |
| Sprint 1 ideas | Brief ideas on features to tackle; any setup still needed |

**No minimum/maximum length.** Be specific and concrete; vague bullet points not useful.

**Deadline:** Sep 17, 11:59 PM

### D7 — Sprint Release (10 points)

**Steps:**
1. Ensure all Sprint 0 PRs merged (or in final reviewed state)
2. Check project's latest release/version tag to find current version number
3. Create Git tag: `<version>-csci435-s0` (do NOT bump version number)
   - Example: current `v2.17.2` → tag as `v2.17.2-csci435-s0`
   - If no prior releases: use `v0.1.0-csci435-s0`
4. Write brief release description of what changed

```bash
git tag v<version>-csci435-s0
git push origin v<version>-csci435-s0
```

Create GitHub release from tag on repository's Releases page.

**Submission:** Link to GitHub release in D6. Tag must be pushed by Sep 17, 11:59 PM.

## What happened

**Install** — no brew on Windows, so it was a manual binary install:
- Downloaded `SpecStoryCLI_Windows_x86_64.zip` (v2.10.0), verified SHA256 against the release's `checksums.txt` — matched.
- It's a single `specstory.exe`, dropped into `C:\Users\carso\.local\bin\`.
- **No PATH edit was needed** — that folder is already on your user PATH (it's where `claude.exe` lives). `specstory` resolves already.
- `specstory check` confirms it found Claude Code 2.1.259 and reports "All systems go."

**The Sep 2 session was not lost.** I was wrong about that earlier — `specstory list` found both sessions, including `Sep 02, 2026 15:19`, the toolchain one. The JSONL I checked had a Sep 3 mtime because that session continued into the next day. `specstory sync` recovered both.

**Content quality is what the spec requires** — not prompt-only. The Sep 2 log is 239 KB with 49 user turns and 228 agent turns, including tool calls, the commands run, and their output inline.

**Filed to the required path** with the required naming:

```
ai-logs/sprint0/CarsonRackley/
  2026-09-02_claude-code_toolchain-setup.md                         (239 KB)
  2026-09-03_claude-code_sprint0-requirements-and-ai-log-setup.md    (60 KB)
```

I also added `.specstory/` to `.git/info/exclude` rather than the tracked `.gitignore` — keeps your local tooling out of git without putting a diff on an upstream file that would show up in your PRs.

## From now on: launch Claude Code as `specstory run claude`

That's the whole habit. Plain `claude` won't wrap the session.

Two things worth knowing:

**Run it from inside the Gitea folder**, not the parent. Your existing sessions were started from `…\Software Engineering\`, so SpecStory associated them with that directory and wrote `.specstory/` there — outside the repo. Starting from `…\Software Engineering\Gitea\` associates future sessions with the repo itself, so `specstory sync` finds them where you need them.

**Re-sync before you submit.** Today's log is a snapshot of a session still in progress, and it'll be incomplete. The course's end-of-sprint checklist says to run `specstory sync` and then rename/move files — so re-run sync near Sep 17 and re-copy.

## Two loose ends

**Cloud sync is unauthenticated** — sync printed a warning. Local markdown generation works fine without it, which is all the course needs. `specstory login` would enable SpecStory Cloud; optional, and I'd skip it unless you want the web UI.

**Slug naming is my judgment call.** The auto-generated names came from first prompts (`is-the-repository-in`), which is uninformative, so I renamed to `toolchain-setup` and `sprint0-requirements-and-ai-log-setup`. The convention only asks for a "short-slug," so rename if you'd describe them differently.

Also, `ai-logs/sprint0/CarsonRackley/` uses your `git config user.name`. If your actual GitHub handle differs, that folder needs renaming — the spec is specific about `<your-github-username>`.

The files are untracked and uncommitted. Want me to commit them (with the `Assisted-by` trailer, no `Co-Authored-By`) on a `chore/` branch, or leave that to you? And note D4 isn't fully closed until the report has your AI-usage summary and your PRs/issues carry the AI Assistance comment table — both of which come later.

AI Log Instructions
&para;
We will provide a Claude subscription to each student. We strongly recommend using this subscription for the class. Using Claude Code CLI is particularly useful because it will facilitate data collection, as documented in these instructions.
While you are encouraged to use Claude, you are free to use any AI tools to assist your work in this class (e.g., when you ran out of tokens with the subscription we provide), on the condition that you
accurately and honestly report your use
. These instructions explain exactly what to log, how to
capture it, and where to submit it.
Don't hesitate to ask questions at any moment, especially during log collection. Contact your TA (
mhasan02@wm.edu
) or
Dr. Chaparro (
oscarch@wm.edu
).
What counts as a loggable session
&para;
Log every AI interaction that is 
related to the course project
, including (but not limited to):
Writing, debugging, or reviewing code
Understanding the codebase, architecture, or an issue
Drafting issue reports, PR descriptions, or documentation
Discussing design decisions or tradeoffs
You do 
not
 need to log: purely academic questions ("explain what a tRPC router is"), general
research unrelated to your project, or assignment instructions you asked AI to clarify.
When in doubt, log it.
Log everything — including unproductive sessions
A session where AI gave wrong answers, went in circles, or didn't help is just as important to document as a productive one. You will not be graded on whether AI was helpful; you will be graded on whether you documented your usage accurately and completely.
Where logs go
&para;
All AI logs live in your team's GitHub repository under:
ai-logs/
  sprint0/
    <your-github-username>/
  sprint1/
    <your-github-username>/
  ...
Each sprint gets its own subfolder. Each team member gets their own subfolder named by their GitHub
username. Create the subfolder if it is not yet present. 
Do not put your logs in a teammate's folder.

Yes — `specstory run claude` is the page's own instruction, verbatim. Here's what it actually says, quoted.

## The page's setup instructions

**Install (Windows):**
> "download `SpecStoryCLI_Windows_x86_64.zip` from the SpecStory releases page, extract to a permanent folder, and add it to your `PATH`. Verify with `specstory version`."

That's exactly what we did — the binary is in `C:\Users\carso\.local\bin` (permanent, already on PATH).

**Usage:**
> ```
> specstory run claude    # instead of: claude
> ```

The comment "*instead of: claude*" is the page's, not mine.

**If you forget to wrap a session:**
> "`specstory sync` … Agentic CLI tools keep their own local session history even when SpecStory isn't wrapping them. `specstory sync` reads those existing records and converts them to SpecStory's Markdown format. Run it after any session you forgot to wrap, **or at any point during a session to pick up turns so far**."

So recovering your Sep 2 session was the documented path, not a lucky workaround.

**End of sprint:**
> "run `specstory sync` one final time, then copy the sprint-related files from `.specstory/history/` into `ai-logs/sprint#/<your-github-username>/`, renaming them to follow the naming convention above. (SpecStory names files by date and tool automatically; **verify that the slug portion describes the session clearly and adjust if needed**.)"

That last clause is why renaming `is-the-repository-in` → `toolchain-setup` was correct rather than presumptuous.

## Where I went beyond the page

**"Run it from inside the Gitea folder" was my advice, not the site's.** The page never mentions working directory. It's still worth doing — SpecStory writes `.specstory/history/` relative to where the session ran, and the page's copy step reads from that folder, so keeping it inside the repo saves you hunting — but don't treat it as a course requirement.

**The copy is meant to happen at the end of the sprint.** The intended flow is: let logs accumulate in `.specstory/history/`, then copy into `ai-logs/` before the deadline. What I did early is a working preview, so re-run sync and re-copy near Sep 17.

## Things the earlier summary dropped that matter

- **The course provides you a Claude subscription** — "We will provide a Claude subscription to each student. We strongly recommend using this subscription." That confirms picking **SEMERUWM** in the Chrome dialog.
- **What to log:** every AI interaction related to the course project — code, understanding the codebase, drafting issues/PRs, design discussions. Not purely academic questions. "When in doubt, log it."
- **Log the failures too**, explicitly: *"A session where AI gave wrong answers, went in circles, or didn't help is just as important to document… You will not be graded on whether AI was helpful; you will be graded on whether you documented your usage accurately and completely."*
- **A log must name the model/tool** (e.g. "Claude Sonnet 4.5 via Claude Code"). SpecStory embeds `claude-opus-5` per turn, so you're covered.
- **Formats:** `.md` preferred, `.txt`/`.json` OK. **No `.docx`, `.pdf`, or `.html`.**
- **"A sharing link is not a log"** — share links expire and can't be analyzed.
- **Claude Desktop isn't captured by SpecStory** — the page recommends switching to Claude Code CLI for project work.
- **Per-issue/PR comment is a required, templated artifact** I'd only mentioned in passing. One comment per contributor per issue, with a `### AI Assistance — @username` heading, a Role line, and a table of `# | Tool | Log | What AI helped with` with repo-relative links. Notably: *"If you had no AI sessions related to this issue, post the comment and note 'No AI used.'"* — so it's required even when AI wasn't used.
- **Questions go to** the TA (mhasan02@wm.edu) or Dr. Chaparro (oscarch@wm.edu).
